rule_hypotheses.rule: 2022-era claims (claim date in 2022) were paid the flat Max Benefit regardless of documentation. Folders often hold only a waiver addendum or cover letter, with no itemization.

Max Benefit = the security deposit waived on the SDRP addendum (9: waived $3,500 = Max 3500). Elsewhere Max is usually the lease deposit or rent rounded up to the next $500 (97: lease SD 2195 -> 2500; 107: lease SD 2475 -> 2500; 82: rent 1695 -> 2000), but 2024 RentWerx/Perry Reid claims show a flat 1500 regardless of rent (417 rent 2700 -> 1500; 764 rent 935 -> 1500; 900 rent 1010 -> 1500).
Core formula: payout = min(sum of covered charges net of tenant payments/credits, Max Benefit [, rent-rounded-up-to-500 cap]).

2023-era (pre-12/1/23) adjusters paid the ledger 'balance due' almost wholesale, including reletting/leasing commission, maintenance coordination fee, PM break-lease fee and pet damage (dog-chewed blinds).

Post-12/2023 exclusions: rent after the lease expiration (month-to-month), late fees, NSF fees, move-out itemization fees, maintenance handling fees, reletting fees, 'security deposit fees', utilities, renters insurance and pet damage. Make-ready repairs, cleaning and trash are covered.

Early lease break (2024): pay rent prorated to the move-out date (monthly rent * days / days in month, rounded to cents) + any unpaid prior-month balance + a lease-break fee of one month's rent + damages. Do NOT pay future rent through the lease end date.
Lease-break fee and early-termination fee (about one month of rent) are covered, but if the tenant already paid them, only the remaining balance is paid.
Eviction / rent default where unpaid rent exceeds the cap is paid at Max Benefit.
Approved amounts sometimes drop the cents (truncated to whole dollars).
Possible 50% payout or keying error: 946 paid exactly half of the balance due, a figure printed on the statement as 'Collection fees'.
Small cleaning-only claims at lease end may be declined (possibly tenant paid, or routine turnover cleaning treated as normal wear); no reason recorded.

extraction_lessons: Excalibur Homes (GA/TN) 'Statement' ledgers list every charge and payment since move-in, with Balance Due in the header. The claimable set is the charges after the last tenant payment, and they sum exactly to Balance Due (82: 4658.50; 97: 225). Monthly 'YRIG Prem' and 'Sec Dep Ins Charge to Tenant' lines are premiums.

Propertyware ledgers (New Heights PM) label rows 'Unpaid Charge' vs 'Paid Charge', and the header gives 'Total Unpaid'. The 'Move-out Repair : #<Meld id>' line equals the separate vendor invoice total, so count the invoice items OR the ledger line, never both (107).

RentWerx itemization letters lump rent and fees into one 'Balance on Ledger' line. The printed 'Total Charges' may not equal the sum of the listed lines (417: 9188.60 vs 9163.00). The adjuster used the 'Make Ready' line only.
zInspector / ManagerServices move-out reports (RentWerx) are condition and photo checklists with no dollar amounts. They cannot drive a computation (417, 633).

Perry Reid 'DD Authorization' PDFs are ACH forms with PM bank details and a template VOID check for $1,234.56 ('Replace windows north side 1000.55', 'Replace carpets downstairs #5 234.01'). OCR must ignore them; they are not claim charges (764, 900).
Perry Reid 'Security Deposit Itemization - Move Out' forms are scanned (need vision). Their Yardi ledger .docx repeats each cell several times because of merged cells; dedupe by row.

Johnson Property Management (Rent Manager) final statements print a hypothetical 'Collection fees' line (50% of balance) and a 'Total amount owed if assigned to collections' line. These are not charges, but in 946 the approved amount equals the collection-fee line.
Vendor invoices can differ from what the PM actually charged the tenant (946: invoice 270 vs charged 220). Prefer the PM statement amounts.

PM Explanation notes sometimes contain arithmetic typos (764: '120.54' where 935*4/31 = 120.65), but the approved amount follows the correct arithmetic. Prorations use monthly rent / days in that month.
Many folders lack the itemization entirely (8, 9, 19, 633, 764). For 2022 claims, pay Max Benefit. For 2024 claims, the PM Explanation is the only usable breakdown.

The workbook 'Comments' sheet is keyed by 'Row N' and is misaligned with the current claim rows: comments dated 2024-25 attach to 2022-23 claims, and their content (e.g. 'benefit should not have exceeded 2500' on claim 82 with Max 2000) does not match. Do not use them per-claim without re-anchoring.

Sheet fields can be wrong. 107 Move-Out Date is 4/30/23 but the ledger prorates May for 18 days. 946 Monthly Rent 1345 includes a $50 amenity package (base rent 1295). Lease-listed deposits (97: 2195; 107: 2475) do not always equal Max Benefit.
Tenant-contact JPG screenshots (Excalibur) and rental applications (RentWerx) contain PII and nothing relevant to the payout. Classify them as 'other' and skip them.
